title: ADC, PWM, and analog input

spans.text: LESSON PURPOSE

Goal: apply “ADC, PWM, and analog input” to a real program or device. The key principle is: PWM duty cycle controls the fraction of time the output is high. In a project, follow this guidance: Use the board's documented ADC range and calibrate raw values to physical units.

CORE EXPLANATION
An ADC converts voltage to a digital value with board-specific range and resolution. PWM modulates a digital output; it is not necessarily a true DAC.
IMPORTANT LINE BREAKDOWN
Key line:
int raw = analogRead(sensorPin);

What it does: PWM duty cycle controls the fraction of time the output is high.
Why it is used: Use the board's documented ADC range and calibrate raw values to physical units.
If omitted or changed: Never connect 5 V directly to a 3.3 V ADC input; check the board's limits.
